title: Steinberg simplicity for a restricted module tensored with a Frobenius pullback
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and such that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], taking the positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$. Let $f:S\to S$ be a surjective $F$-group-scheme homomorphism with finite scheme-theoretic kernel such that $f(T)\subseteq T$, $f(U)\subseteq U$ and
$$\chi\circ f|_T=p\chi\quad\text{for every }\chi\in X.$$
Here finite kernel means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and the subgroup containments are factorizations of scheme morphisms. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $M$ with a coassociative counital coaction $c_M:M\to M\otimes_F F[S]$. A submodule is a linear subspace stable under this coaction, and simple means nonzero with only zero and itself as submodules. Put $M^U=\{m:c_M|_U(m)=m\otimes1\}$. A simple module has highest weight $\eta\in X$ when $M^U$ is one-dimensional and $T$ acts on this line by $\eta$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Let $V,W$ be finite-dimensional simple rational $S$-modules with highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in X$. Assume $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are dominant, meaning nonnegative pairing with every simple coroot, and assume $0\le\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle<p$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$. Define $f^*W$ to have exactly the vector space $W$, with coaction $(1\otimes f^\#)c_W$, where $f^\#:F[S]\to F[S]$ is pullback of regular functions. Give $V\otimes_F f^*W$ its diagonal coaction, equivalently
$$s\cdot(v\otimes w)=(s\cdot v)\otimes(f(s)\cdot w)$$
after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Then $V\otimes_F f^*W$ is a simple rational $S$-module. This includes $p=2$, zero highest weights, products of simple groups and $S=1$.

source.place: Part II, 3.16--3.17, Steinberg tensor product theorem (simplicity formulation). WANTED: book not local. Online corroboration read: Williamson, Algebraic representations and constructible sheaves, arXiv:1610.06261v1, section 1.4, Theorem 1.3, printed p.6, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.06261. Extension from the split-model Frobenius to any f inducing p on X uses Milne, Algebraic Groups, Theorem 23.25, printed pp.492--493 (uniqueness up to inner torus automorphism). The positive Borel convention concerns U-highest lines, not the negative Borel used for induction in Williamson section 1.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-p-isogeny-relative-frobenius] to $S,T,f$: $S$ is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and the finite-kernel, surjectivity and torus hypotheses are exactly those given. Obtain $f=hF_{S/F}$ with $h$ an isomorphism. The coordinate algebra $C=F[S]$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] applied to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. The map $F_{S/F}^{\#}:C\otimes_{F,\mathrm{Frob}}F\to C$ is injective: choose $p$th roots in $F$; every $\sum_i b_i\otimes c_i$ equals $(\sum_i c_i^{1/p}b_i)\otimes1$, whose image is $(\sum_i c_i^{1/p}b_i)^p$. Reducedness makes a zero image imply a zero tensor. Thus $f^\#$ is injective. On dual-number points $b(e+\varepsilon x)=\epsilon(b)+\varepsilon x(b)$, taking $p$th powers removes the $\varepsilon$ term. Hence $F_{S/F}(e+\varepsilon x)=e$ and $f(e+\varepsilon x)=e$ for every tangent vector $x$; equivalently $df=0$.

source.place: 2.25--2.29 and 23.25--23.26; elementary coordinate consequences of the cited Frobenius factorization. Reducedness: Stacks Tag 056T, varieties.tex, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak s=\operatorname{Lie}(S)$, defined by the augmentation derivations in [lem-sfb-restricted-module-infinitesimal-simplicity]. Since $\lambda$ is dominant and $p$-restricted and $V$ is finite-dimensional simple with the specified $U$-highest line, that node applies and makes $V$ infinitesimally simple. Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_F(V)$ be the unital $F$-subalgebra generated by all $d\rho_V(x)$ for $x\in\mathfrak s$. An $A$-submodule is automatically an $F$-subspace, because $A$ contains the scalar operators; stability under $A$ is equivalent to stability under these generators. Consequently $V$ is a faithful simple left $A$-module. By [lem-sfb-simple-algebra-scalar-endomorphisms], $C_A=\operatorname{End}_A(V)$ consists exactly of scalar maps. Any finite $F$-basis of $V$ therefore generates it over $C_A$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-simple-double-centralizer]: every $F$-linear endomorphism of $V$, being $C_A$-linear, is the action of an element of $A$. The action is the inclusion, so $A=\operatorname{End}_F(V)$.

source.place: 22.54, printed p.481; 14.1, printed pp.279--280, scalar Schur and finite double-centralizer argument.

proof.text: Let $N\subseteq V\otimes_F f^*W$ be an $S$-submodule. Evaluate its coaction on the dual-number point $e+\varepsilon x$. Since $df=0$, its action on $f^*W$ is the identity, while its action on $V$ is $1+\varepsilon d\rho_V(x)$. Comparing coefficients of $\varepsilon$ gives $(d\rho_V(x)\otimes1)N\subseteq N$. Stability under sums, scalar multiples and products now gives $(a\otimes1)N\subseteq N$ for every $a\in A=\operatorname{End}_F(V)$. Choose a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of the nonzero space $V$ and put $Z=\{w\in W:v_1\otimes w\in N\}$. For $n=\sum_i v_i\otimes w_i\in N$, applying the matrix unit $E_{1i}$ puts $v_1\otimes w_i$ in $N$, so every $w_i$ lies in $Z$. Conversely, $w\in Z$ implies $v_j\otimes w\in N$ by $E_{j1}$. Thus $N=V\otimes_F Z$ as subspaces, by the explicit two inclusions.

source.place: 22(e), differential action and the tensor argument underlying 22.55; explicit dual-number and matrix-unit calculation.

proof.text: For every commutative $F$-algebra $R$, scalar extension identifies $N_R$ with $V_R\otimes_R Z_R$ (extend a basis of $Z$ to one of $W$). Its stability under $\rho_V(s)\otimes\rho_W(f(s))$, for $s\in S(R)$, and its stability under $\rho_V(s)^{-1}\otimes1$ imply stability under $1\otimes\rho_W(f(s))$. Applying the first basis-coordinate functional on $V_R$ to $v_1\otimes z$ shows $\rho_W(f(s))Z_R\subseteq Z_R$. In particular take $R=F[S]$ and the universal $S$-point corresponding to the identity of $F[S]$. This says exactly that $(1\otimes f^\#)c_W(Z)\subseteq Z\otimes F[S]$, so $Z$ is a rational submodule of $f^*W$. Let $\pi:W\to W/Z$. For $z\in Z$, put $u=(\pi\otimes1)c_W(z)\in(W/Z)\otimes F[S]$. The inclusion just proved says $(1\otimes f^\#)u=0$. Since $f^\#$ is injective, so is $1\otimes f^\#$: expand in a basis of $W/Z$. Therefore $u=0$ for every $z$, and $Z$ is a submodule of $W$ itself. Simplicity gives $Z=0$ or $W$, hence $N=0$ or $V\otimes f^*W$. The tensor space is nonzero because $V,W$ have nonzero basis vectors. It is therefore simple. All arguments allow $d=1$, $p=2$, zero weights and $S=1$.
